Alex / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Per our conversation I attached an initial throughput model (orbit_throughput_model_q4_v3.xlsx) that maps your reported traffic patterns to dedicated slab sizing, with conservative headroom assumptions for bursts and cold starts. High-level asks from our side so we can finalize the Dedicated proposal: 

- Confirm target SLOs: p50/p95 generation latency targets and acceptable tail (we currently assume p95 <= 250ms for your shorter prompts, p95 <= 600ms for long-context retrieval flows).
- Share observed tokens/sec at peak (10/90/99 percentiles) and a daily hourly distribution if available.
- Any constraints on quantization/precision (INT8 allowed?) or hard no-quantization for quality.
- Procurement timeline / desired start date for reserved capacity.

Prelim notes in the spreadsheet: we model three operating modes — steady-state, burst (1.5–2x steady peak for 30–90s), and cold-start recovery. For your reported sample of ~65k tokens/sec peak (from the demo logs), the model recommends 6x A100-40 slabs in dedicated with a 20% burst buffer and active KV prefix caching. That yields p95 projections around 220–280ms depending on quantization and KV hit rate.

I'm looping Priyom (inference) and Kim (solutions) to add technical and commercial constraints. Let's slot a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to walk through the workbook.

Alex / team —

I dug into the spreadsheet and the sample histogram. Below is a short technical summary and concrete sizing math (keeps assumptions explicit):

Assumptions:
- Baseline model: 40B decoder (FP16) with optimized kernels on A100-40 (baseline single-token latency ~0.6ms at low batch; throughput scales with batching and KV cache hit rate).
- KV/prefix caching: assume 75% hit for warm conversational flows; cold path cost is ~2.2x token compute due to context re-encoding.
- Quantization/Perf delta: INT8 gives ~1.6x token/sec improvement but with slight quality risk; FP16 baseline used for formal SLA.
- Burst profile: 110k tokens/sec (99th) sustained for <= 60s; planning buffer for 2x steady peak for safety.

Sizing calc (simplified):
- Measured sustained capacity per A100-40 slab (FP16, mixed batching, 1 active stream per GPU pool) ≈ 13k tokens/sec effective with KV caching at 75%.
- For 78k tokens/sec sustained peak → 78k / 13k ≈ 6.0 slabs.
- Add 20% burst buffer for headroom and autoscaling ramping → 6.0 * 1.2 ≈ 7.2 → round to 8 slabs to give margin and allow rolling upgrades.
- Cold-start cushion / pre-warm shards: reserve 1 slab as warm-backfill to shorten cold recovery; this reduces observed p95 during ramp.

Projected latency (p95):
- FP16, 75% KV hit, 8 slabs → p95 ~ 240ms for short prompts (matches your customer-facing SLO).
- If we must avoid INT8 entirely and your KV hit is lower (50%), p95 could drift to ~330–380ms during sustained peaks.

Recommendations:
1) Commit to 8 slabs A100-40 as the Dedicated offer; include a 30% burst pool available for short surges (Doc: orbit_throughput_model_q4_v3.xlsx).
2) Implement aggressive prefix/KV warming for the campaign windows — pre-warm window 5–10 minutes before expected peak time slots.
3) Offer a lower-cost INT8 lane for non-customer-facing workloads; this can reduce committed slab count by ~1–2 if adopted.
4) Include a scheduled canary (1–2 slabs) during rollout and a monitoring hook to auto-fallback to hosted model if SLOs degrade.

I also attached a thermal map (thermal_gpu_map_diagram.png) that correlates slab count to expected power/thermal profile for planning on customer hardware racks (for private deployment discussion).

— Priyom
